# mv

Move or rename files and directories through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/mv old.txt new.txt

moonx cli/mv -n report.txt archive/

moonx cli/mv --backup=simple report.txt archive/
```

Move a source to a destination, or multiple sources into a directory. Select overwrite, update and backup behavior explicitly.

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--force` | Replace without asking. |
| `-n`, `--no-clobber` | Skip existing targets successfully. |
| `-i`, `--interactive` | Ask before replacing; refusal or EOF returns 1. |
| `--update=MODE` | Select the documented destination update policy. |
| `--backup=CONTROL` | Select the documented backup naming policy. |
| `-T`, `--no-target-directory` | Treat target as a complete path; one source only. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Show moves. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

Use `--help` for the complete option list.

## Notes

- Cross-filesystem moves are unsupported. Windows rejects moving symlinks/junctions and backing up destination links.
- -i and -u reject equal source/target timestamps. Same-file moves fail except for explicit skip modes.
- If both a move and backup restoration fail, inspect the destination and backup paths named in the diagnostic before retrying.

Build from source with the MoonBit 1.0 RC1 toolchain.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
